breaking.headline: Futures sink as tariff reports and the chip rout deepen the AI selloff
breaking.fact: Nasdaq 100 futures fell more than 2% and S&P 500 futures about 1.3-2% overnight after Reuters reported the Trump administration is poised to unveil Section 301 tariff findings on 16 economies, with the EU, Japan and South Korea capped at 15% under trade deals and China, India and Vietnam facing higher rates. Nvidia fell about 5% premarket to near $147 after Tuesday's 5.9% drop, and the VIX is back above 30.

breaking.headline: Deere misses and cuts its 2027 outlook as farm demand stays soft
breaking.fact: Deere reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $3.89 a share, below the $4.07 analysts expected, though revenue of $10.5 billion topped estimates. The farm-equipment maker issued a disappointing 2027 outlook, with CEO John May blaming continued uncertainty in key end markets, and shares fell about 2% premarket.

breaking.headline: PCE and GDP land at 8:30 AM with a December hike nearly a certainty
breaking.fact: October PCE inflation, the second estimate of third-quarter GDP, durable goods orders and jobless claims all land at 8:30 AM ET, the last big data dump before the Fed's December meeting. PCE is expected at 0.3% for the month and 3.8% over the year, with core at 3.2%. Fed funds futures price a 97% chance of a December hike and 63% for another in January. Markets are closed Thursday and shut early Friday.

breaking.headline: Two million Thanksgiving travelers to pass through Houston's airports
breaking.fact: Houston Airports expects about two million passengers through Bush Intercontinental (1.6 million) and Hobby (443,000) during the Thanksgiving travel period through Nov 30, with Wednesday the busiest day for departures. TxDOT warns of heavy congestion on I-45 from noon to 8 PM and I-10 from 11 AM to 8 PM today.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed Tuesday in Paris at €188.12, worth $206.24 at the ECB's Nov 24 reference rate of 1.0963, up a half percent in dollars. The industrial-gas giant keeps grinding steadily higher while U.S. tech gives back Monday's rally, its defensive profile doing the quiet work. With no company news, the dollar price mostly tracks the euro near the top of its recent range.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic fell 6.5% Tuesday to $81.91, closing below its $83 IPO price for the first time as the debut euphoria faded. The AI name got swept up in the chip selloff as investors questioned whether the debt-fueled AI spending boom will pay off. Sean's IPO allocation is underwater on paper, but this is a long-term hold, not a trade. Watch whether the stock can reclaim the IPO price once the selling eases.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up a penny Tuesday to $91.61, doing what a Treasury-bill fund should do while growth stocks slid. The fund's $0.30849 distribution, ex Nov 2 and paid Nov 5, carries a 4.04% distribution yield. With the Fed now seen as nearly certain to hike in December, short-term Treasury yields stay supported. BIL remains the quiet, government-cash anchor of the watchlist, untouched by the AI drama.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet slipped 1.1% Tuesday to $279.05, giving back part of Monday's rally as the Nasdaq fell 1.5% and chips led the decline. The AI spending question hanging over the market cuts both ways for Google: its cloud business benefits, but the capital outlays keep growing. Futures point lower this morning ahead of the PCE report. The AI and search thesis is intact, but the tape is rough into the holiday.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly jumped 3.2% Tuesday to $1,407.59, one of the day's strongest large caps while tech slid, as money rotated to defensive growth. Moody's lifted Lilly to Aa2 this week, citing the weight-loss drug franchise's growth. With the Fed leaning hawkish, Lilly's drug-driven earnings look comparatively safe. The stock remains near the top of its range, and the GLP-1 story still has room to run.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere Energy inched up 0.2% Tuesday to $296.01, steady while oil whipsawed and the broader market fell. Natural-gas export demand stays firm, and the Strait of Hormuz tensions keep energy in focus, though Cheniere's U.S. Gulf Coast terminals sit far from the strait. The stock has been a quiet outperformer this fall. Watch the OPEC+ meeting this weekend and winter gas demand for the next move.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia dropped 5.9% Tuesday to $155.38, giving back part of Monday's 31% surge after Huang's reinstatement, and down about 5% more premarket to near $147. The chip rout deepened overnight on tariff reports and doubts about AI spending payoffs. Sean's call stands: a long-term hold until the probes and investigation shake out, with Huang testifying Dec 1. The next real test is the 8:30 AM PCE print.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer climbed 3.9% Tuesday to $28.46, a strong day as investors rotated into defensive dividend payers. The drugmaker's yield and steady cash flow look attractive with the Fed leaning toward another hike and growth stocks under pressure. Pfizer remains well off its highs, and the dividend is the core of the thesis here. Watch for any pipeline or deal news to give the stock a second leg.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab sank 7.4% Tuesday to $45.98, caught in the growth-stock downdraft as the Nasdaq fell 1.5%. The space stock has been volatile all month, swinging with risk appetite rather than company news. No fresh launch or contract headlines drove the move; it was the tape. The long-term launch-cadence story is unchanged, but the stock needs calmer markets to find a footing.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital jumped 6.3% Tuesday to $8.67, one of the day's best performers while the market fell, as the mortgage REIT's dividend yield drew buyers. Higher-for-longer rates are a mixed blessing for Rithm: they pressure book value but fatten the spreads on new investments. The stock has been climbing steadily this month. Watch the December Fed decision and mortgage-rate direction for the next leg.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX, the leveraged S&P 500 fund, fell 5.7% Tuesday to $125.81, tracking the market's slide with its usual amplified move as the S&P 500 lost 0.5%. Leveraged funds magnify both directions, and this week has been all downside for the tape. The position is a trading vehicle, not a buy-and-hold, and sharp down days are the cost of the leverage. Watch the PCE print at 8:30 AM for the next swing.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist Financial rose 1.3% Tuesday to $47.48, holding up as the Dow climbed above 50,000 for the first time and banks caught a bid. Regional banks benefit from the steepening rate outlook as the Fed leans hawkish, and Truist's dividend adds ballast. The stock has been grinding higher this month while tech whipsaws. Watch the PCE report and the December Fed meeting for the rate path driving bank earnings.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony plunged 8.8% Tuesday to $2.18, giving back part of its recent bounce as small miners sold off. China's antimony and chip-material export curbs stay on hold until January, so no new policy pressure, but the stock trades on sentiment. The long-term domestic-supply thesis is intact, and the company remains a speculative bet. Watch for defense or critical-minerals news to spark the next move.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy fell 4.6% Tuesday to $5.57, sliding with the broader market despite no company-specific news. The uranium story still rests on nuclear expansion and government buying, but the stock is hostage to risk appetite in the meantime. UEC remains a favorite long-term holding, and Sean wants to add while the price is low. Watch for reactor or contracting headlines and the general turn in sentiment.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero Energy slipped 1.4% Tuesday to $324.67 even as the Dow hit 50,000, as oil seesawed and refiners gave back gains. Brent settled Tuesday at $91.40 but has since faded toward $89 on surplus worries ahead of the OPEC+ weekend meeting. Valero's refining margins remain the swing factor, and the dividend keeps paying while the stock consolidates. Watch OPEC+ and winter fuel demand for direction.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Vanguard Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV slipped to $28.43 as of Nov 24, down 0.3% as stocks fell and bonds held steady. The diversified target-date fund does the quiet work of the portfolio, blending U.S. and international stocks with bonds that glide more conservative over time. Tuesday's dip was modest beside the Nasdaq's 1.5% slide. It remains a set-and-forget core holding for the 2035 horizon.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC is estimated at $148.02, down 0.5% on the S&P 500's Tuesday slide, using the S&P-anchored estimator recalibrated from Sean's account value. The fund tracks the broad market, so its move simply mirrors the index, which fell as tech gave back Monday's gains. The estimate updates with each S&P close and stays marked as an estimate. Watch the PCE report this morning for the market's next direction.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.78% as published Nov 24. The sweep fund keeps shrinking by design: whenever it tops $1,000 in an account, the cash moves into a CD, and the position should evaporate over time. The yield trails Vanguard's Treasury fund, but SWVXX remains the Schwab sweep vehicle. Leftover pennies go to the mutual-fund remnants once an account is near zero.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.04% as published Nov 24, up a touch from 4.03%. The Treasury money-market fund is the eTrade cash home and the landing spot for the Seiver Slough and Seiver Lodge sale proceeds down the road. It pays more than Schwab's SWVXX and carries no ticket fee at eTrade. The yield should stay supported with a December Fed hike now nearly certain.

weekInBrief.headline: Dell beats big — and sinks anyway as the AI selloff spares no one
weekInBrief.body: Dell reported a blowout quarter — adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share on revenue of $54.9 billion, roughly double a year ago — raised full-year revenue guidance to $202 billion and added $25 billion to its buyback. The Round Rock, Texas server maker still fell about 6% premarket, swept up in the AI selloff, and its 36% November slide is on track for the worst month in its history.

weekInBrief.headline: Oil slides on surplus fears ahead of the OPEC+ weekend meeting
weekInBrief.body: Brent crude settled Tuesday at $91.40 but faded toward $89 overnight as traders weighed expectations of a global supply surplus ahead of OPEC+'s meeting this weekend, with the renewed Hormuz shipping tensions competing against the glut. WTI held near $82. The surplus outlook, not the strait, is setting the price for now.

weekInBrief.headline: Workday drops 7.7% as a soft backlog overshadows a solid quarter
weekInBrief.body: Workday posted solid third-quarter earnings with strong AI enterprise-software revenue, but a weak total subscription backlog gave investors a reason to sell, and shares fell 7.7%. The human-resources software maker is the latest enterprise name to be punished for guidance rather than results in a market that is repricing AI spending.

weekInBrief.headline: Autodesk beats and raises guidance as design software holds up
weekInBrief.body: Autodesk earned $3.20 a share in its fiscal third quarter, beating the $3.07 analysts expected, on revenue of $2.16 billion versus $2.13 billion expected, and raised its full-year earnings guidance. The design-software maker stood out on a day when most tech names fell, showing that not every software story is tied to the AI infrastructure trade.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait early Wednesday, the Revolutionary Guards navy said, claiming the vessels were on an unauthorized route — the latest in a near-daily string of mine incidents this month. Iran's army chief on Tuesday ordered the navy to tighten the closure 'further day by day' until Washington meets Tehran's conditions, while Tehran told Washington through Qatari mediators it would reopen the waterway within 48 hours if its demands — lifting the U.S. naval blockade and ending the war on all fronts — are met. U.S. Central Command has denied Iranian claims that U.S.-escorted tankers hit mines, saying the primary shipping lanes are clear. Iranian crude exports remain near zero — Kpler puts 40 to 50 million barrels of Iranian oil still on the water in Asia, discharging in China at close to 1 million barrels a day — while non-Iranian Gulf oil keeps flowing at roughly 70% of pre-war volumes.

space.headline: Flight 17 hardware finishes cryo tests as Starship's next campaign takes shape
space.body: Both Starship Flight 17 vehicles have finished cryogenic proof testing at Massey's and rolled back to the production site: Ship 44 completed its third cryo test early Tuesday, and Super Heavy Booster 24 finished its first round of testing on Monday. SpaceX has still not announced a date for Flight 16 — unofficial estimates put it around mid-January — or for Flight 17, and has not named the vehicles. The next steps are engine tests and stacking.

space.headline: Rice catalyst splits CO2 with visible light — no furnace needed
space.body: Rice University researchers have shown a way to split carbon dioxide using visible light and no external heating, pairing light-harvesting copper nanoparticles with cerium oxide, which traps the freed oxygen so the catalyst can be reused. Under blue light the system produced carbon monoxide at 15,000 micromoles per hour per gram for nearly four hours. The work, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, is licensed to Houston-based Syzygy Plasmonics.

space.headline: Blood test maps how small cell lung cancer dodges a new drug
space.body: Dana-Farber researchers used a blood test plus new mouse models to track how small cell lung cancer responds to tarlatamab and how it escapes. Patients whose tumors carried the ASCL1 profile were far more likely to benefit — 16 of 20 saw clinical benefit, with a median 9.6 months before progression, versus about two months for other subtypes. Tumors escaped either by shifting subtype and losing the DLL3 target, or by exhausting nearby T cells. The study was published in Cancer Cell.

space.headline: Webb reveals new details in supernova remnant Cassiopeia A
space.body: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has produced a high-resolution, mid-infrared view of the hot dust inside Cassiopeia A, the remnant of a massive star that exploded about 340 years ago. The image, released Nov 23, supports a scenario in which the star's interior underwent a dramatic change just hours before it died. Remnants like Cas A seed new generations of stars and planets with the heavy elements forged in the explosion.

apod.title: SPHEREx Seeing Through Dust
apod.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech SPHEREx; data from NASA/IPAC IRSA. Processing: The Bright Nobles (Muhammet Mücahit Soylu, Serdar Aydın, Furkan Küpeli), ChronosphereX
apod.explanation: What is blocking the center of the Milky Way? This still from today's SPHEREx video shows infrared light from the Galactic Center at 1.2 microns, where the view is almost entirely blocked by clouds of cosmic dust — near-infrared light gets absorbed and scatters off dust grains. At longer, mid-infrared wavelengths the light pierces the dust and the center shines through, the same reason sunsets look red. SPHEREx maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colors, turning dust from an obstacle into a tool for reading the galaxy.
